messages.author: 4326e8dca5f40560
messages.subject: Crash of Rgui
parts:
Hi all 
I'm trying to implement a meta-analysis model, but for a reason I do not understand, Rstan crashes Rgui.exe under windows 7 when running the random effects model.
I must be doing something wrong but I can't see what.
TIA
Jacques

*********************************************
t1 <- c(1,1,1,1,1,3,3,4,4)
t2 <- c(3,3,3,2,2,4,4,5,5)
y <- c(-1.22, -16, -2,-0.7, -0.3, -0.24, -0.73, -20.2, -21.8)
se <- c(0.504, 0.07, 0.07, 0.282, 0.505, 0.265, 0.335, 0.197, 0.2)

N <- length(t1)
nt <- 5; 
data <- list(N = N, nt = nt, t1= t1, t2=t2, y = y , se=se)


library(rstan)

model_code <- '
data {
    int <lower=1> N;
    int <lower=1> nt;
    int <lower=1> t1[N]; 
    int <lower=1> t2[N]; 
    real y[N]; 
    real se[N]; 
  }

  parameters {
    real d[nt];
    real <lower=0, upper=5> se_delta; 
}

  model {
    real delta[N]; 
    real mu[N]; 
    real nd[nt]; 
    se_delta~uniform(0,5);

    for (k in 2:nt){
       d[k]~normal(0, 100) ;
    }
    d[1]~normal(0, 0.0000001) ;

    for (i in 1:N){
       mu[i] <- d[t2[i]] - d[t1[i]];
  //    delta[i] ~ normal(mu[i], se_delta); // <<=== This line makes Rgui.  crash
  //    y[i]~normal(delta[i], se[i]); 
     y[i]~normal(mu[i], se[i]); 
    }

}

generated quantities {
real D12 ;
real D13 ;
real D23 ;
real D45 ;
D12 <- d[1] - d[2];
D13 <- d[1] - d[3];
D23 <- d[2] - d[3];
D45 <- d[4] - d[5];


}
'

fit <- stan(model_code = model_code, data = data, iter = 1000, chains = 4)

messages.author: 0839befa8a8b7d53
messages.subject: Re: Crash of Rgui
parts: I think the issue might be that you need to define the array delta in the parameters block, not as a local in the model block. i.e. move "real delta[N];" to the parameters block. I think that'll fix the crash, but I haven't looked closely enough to verify the model would behave as you intend.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Crash of Rgui
parts:
On Monday, November 26, 2012 2:29:31 PM UTC-5, jr wrote:
I'm trying to implement a meta-analysis model, but for a reason I do not understand, Rstan crashes Rgui.exe under windows 7 when running the random effects model.
I must be doing something wrong but I can't see what.

As Richard pointed out, the source of the crash is having Delta in the wrong block. But the model could be improved and made more efficient by avoiding trying to literally translate BUGS code:
 
  model {
    real delta[N];  // move to parameters block to avoid crash
    real mu[N];
    real nd[nt];    // not used?
    se_delta~uniform(0,5); // not explicitly necessary when support is bounded to (0,5)

d[k]~normal(0, 100) ; // could vectorize with some effort  
    }
    d[1]~normal(0, 0.0000001) ; // likely a mistake: remember Stan uses a mean and standard deviation parameterization
                                                // or maybe you intended to fix d[1] to zero?

for (i in 1:N){
       mu[i] <- d[t2[i]] - d[t1[i]];

//   delta[i] ~ normal(mu[i], se_delta); // slow
   //   y[i]~normal(delta[i], se[i]);           // slow
    }
    delta ~ normal(mu, se_delta); // faster
       y ~ normal(delta, se);            // faster
}
 
Ben
